summary: Redwood AE/SE walked FinSight through migration parity (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together => Redwood API), demoed Console and Optimize recommendations, and discussed security and perf benchmark next steps. Customer is evaluating parity for chat completions, function calling, and embeddings; main concerns: latency, cost, and SOC2/KMS for PII. Agreed to run a benchmark and exchange mapping spreadsheet.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Park (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood Solutions), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Product); Alice Morgan (FinSight Head of ML), Ravi Patel (FinSight Platform), Sofia Lee (FinSight Security), Tom Nguyen (CTO)

[00:00:04] Maya: ok hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood, i'll kick off, uh quick round robin?
[00:00:11] Alice: hi yeah alice here, head of ml at finsight, primarily evaluating migration impact for our chat assistant product
[00:00:18] Ravi: ravi, platform, looking at infra and cost implications
[00:00:22] Sofia: sofia from security, mostly controls/KMS questions
[00:00:26] Tom: tom, CTO, short on time, mainly listening for risk and cost
[00:00:31] Maya: perfect, thanks. David i'll hand over to you for a live demo - we're focused on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together into Redwood.
[00:00:41] David: great, thanks. ok i'm sharing screen, you should see the Redwood Console - small chance of typo in logo here - um top-left model catalog. First thing, parity: we map OpenAI chat/completions and Anthropic's Claude-like tokens to our unified /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints.
[00:01:05] Ravi: quick q - how do you surface model fallbacks? we have burst traffic and want graceful degradation.
[00:01:12] David: good call, we expose routing policies per route - you can set primary model, then fallback to cheaper quantized variant or another region. The console shows a policy rule: latency < 200ms then use x, else fallback to y. small typo in the label but you get the idea.
[00:01:35] [00:01:36] Alice: and function calling - we currently use OpenAI "functions" heavily for structured output. parity there?
[00:01:43] David: yes, we support function/tool calling semantics - it's very similar to OpenAI but with stronger typing support and structured output enforcement. Example on screen: we define a schema, Redwood will validate and return a tool call event. There might be minor differences in the webhook payload names, we'll include mapping table.
[00:02:04] Maya: i'll upload that parity table after the call - columns: openai param -> redwood param -> example curl.
[00:02:11] Carlos: and embeddings - we saw you mentioned both OpenAI and Together embeddings in the pre-call notes. how's compatibility?
[00:02:18] David: we expose /v1/embeddings with model aliases, most customers see near identical vectors vs OpenAI for like-for-like models. Our optimize layer recommends quantized embeddings for vector DBs to cut cost. there's occasional small vector drift depending on model family.
[00:02:36] Ravi: when you say "near identical" any numbers? cosine > 0.98 or?
[00:02:41] David: usually 0.95-0.99 depending on prompt preproc - we'll run an eval on your sample dataset as a follow-up.
[00:02:49] [00:03:02] Sofia: quick sec - security: do you support customer-managed keys / KMS and VPC peering?
[00:03:08] Maya: yes - Private offers customer-managed KMS and VPC/on-prem options. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK integrations; i'll share SOC2 artifacts as a link.
[00:03:22] Sofia: any audit log retention windows? we need 12 months.
[00:03:26] Lena: audit logs are configurable; enterprise plan supports 12+ months retention and streaming to customer S3 or SIEM.
[00:03:33] Tom: is there a perf cost for KMS on each token or is it session-based?
[00:03:38] David: KMS ops are at key unwrap time, not per-token. there's negligible per-token overhead - main perf cost is inter-region latency if SSF is far.
[00:03:48] [00:04:10] Alice: can you show a real migration example - like a prompt that goes from openai chat->redwood with function call and same response?
[00:04:17] David: yep, switching to a code example. On the left is OpenAI request - messages + functions; on the right is Redwood /v1/chat with nearly identical payload: role/message array, functions schema, and call. The response on screen shows a tool call 'create_ticket' with args. Some key diffs: param names for max_tokens -> max_output_tokens, and temperature -> temp (we'll include mapping).
[00:04:44] Ravi: ok will that break our existing wrappers? we have internal SDK that assumes openai param names.
[00:04:50] David: minimal change - either a thin adapter or we can support an OpenAI-compat endpoint for a short pilot. note: compatibility layer has rate-limit differences.
[00:05:03] [00:05:30] Alice: cost - you said optimize suggests batching and quantization. can you show a concrete before/after?
[00:05:36] Lena: sure - here's an Optimize suggestion card: for your 1k-reqs/min chat pattern, we recommend 16 token batch window and int8 quantization for the model variant, projected 37% cost savings while latency stays within SLA for 80th percentile. small asterisk: not all models hit same savings.
[00:05:58] Ravi: how intrusive is quantization? we'd need to validate quality regression on our eval set.
[00:06:03] David: exactly - we integrate eval runs. Redwood Optimize can run A/B tests and surface regressions per prompt set; you keep the quality gates.
[00:06:14] [00:06:45] Sofia: another security detail - does Redwood store user data by default? our legal says we must not persist PII beyond 30 days unless encrypted with BYOK.
[00:06:53] Maya: default retention for hosted is 30 days, enterprise can configure retention policies and BYOK; we also offer onboarded erase APIs.
[00:07:02] Tom: okay good.
[00:07:08] David: switching to routing and rollouts: Console lets you create per-route configs, canary/baseline, automatic rollback if error % > threshold. This helps you migrate gradually from OpenAI to Redwood.
[00:07:25] Alice: what about inference speed - our current OpenAI 1k token median is ~120ms on average. can you match that?
[00:07:34] David: depends on model and region. For hosted low-latency instances we target comparable latencies; Dedicated gives more predictable p95. We'll need to run your payload with our runtime to confirm, but typical 1k token med around 100-160ms for similar architectures on our service.
[00:07:54] [00:08:20] Ravi: do you have a quick-start script to swap endpoints? we want minimal code changes for our infra team.
[00:08:25] Maya: yes - i'll share a repo with example adapters: openai->redwood shim, plus k8s ingress and sample rate-limiter config.
[00:08:33] Carlos: also note model naming conventions - we alias models to easy names (e.g., redwood-gpt-1 -> openai-compat-1) to simplify mapping.
[00:08:44] Alice: great. On evaluation, we want to run a bench: quality + latency + cost. can you run a sample using our anonymized prompt set?
[00:08:53] David: absolutely, we'll run a benchmark, we'll need the dataset and expected metrics - accuracy/ROUGE or human eval?
[00:08:59] Alice: initial automated metrics plus a small human sample.
[00:09:03] David: sounds good, we'll scope that in the follow-up.
[00:09:12] [00:09:40] Sofia: about compliance - SSO, RBAC, SCIM?
[00:09:45] Maya: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in Console. We'll share configuration docs.
[00:09:56] Ravi: you're mentioning Dedicated - cost model there? monthly reserved plus burst?
[00:10:02] Lena: Dedicated has reserved GPU pools with optional burst capacity; pricing is commit-based, we can model it against your usage. For short pilots Hosted with committed burst sometimes cheaper.
[00:10:18] [00:10:55] Tom: any gotchas migrating models that rely on Anthropic safety layers?
[00:11:02] David: Anthropic has unique safety patterns; Redwood provides built-in safety hooks and you can plug annotated classifiers. There may be small diffs - we'll map those in the parity doc.
[00:11:12] Alice: ok, pivot to embeddings integration - we use Pinecone; do you have native connectors or do we continue using our current vector db?
[00:11:20] David: we have connectors to major vector DBs, but you can keep Pinecone seamlessly. Our SDK also has async bulk embedding helpers.
[00:11:30] [00:11:55] Maya: quick demo of Console routing UI - creating a route, selecting model, adding rollout 10% canary - you can see traffic split and realtime token spend. small transcription glitch - you'll see a chart update in real time.
[00:12:20] Ravi: nice, that spend by token at route level helps.
[00:12:25] David: also Optimize shows recommendations: batching, cache prefixes for long chats, and KV cache reuse between similar sessions.
[00:12:36] Alice: KV cache - how do you handle security for cached prefixes with sensitive data?
[00:12:42] David: cache encryption and TTLs, plus access control - you can disable prefix caching for sensitive routes.
[00:12:50] [00:13:30] Sofia: legal will want encryption-at-rest proofs and key rotation policy.
[00:13:35] Maya: we'll include rotation docs and our KMS integration whitepaper.
[00:13:40] David: quick note on observed regressions: Optimize flags prompts where quantized model deviates beyond threshold and can auto route those through a higher fidelity model.
[00:13:56] [00:14:30] Alice: are there SDK language parity issues? we use node and python currently.
[00:14:35] Carlos: we have official SDKs in node/python/go and an openai-compat shim for short term.
[00:14:42] Ravi: rate limits - do you have per-route or per-key throttles?
[00:14:47] David: both - per-key quotas and per-route burst limits, and token-level accounting exposed in Console.
[00:15:00] [00:15:40] Maya: ok summary - action items: we'll send parity mapping spreadsheet, security pack, and example shim repo. Redwood runs a perf bench on your sample set and returns results.
[00:15:52] Alice: sounds good, timeline - can we have the bench by next tuesday?
[00:15:57] David: we'll aim for results by 2026-12-16, that work for you?
[00:16:02] Alice: yes.
[00:16:07] Sofia: also please include privacy dataflow diagram in the pack.
[00:16:11] Maya: will do.
[00:16:30] [00:17:00] Tom: any final pricing notes? initial pilot - hosted trial credits?
[00:17:05] Lena: we'll propose a trial package: hosted credits + small Dedicated trial option. Maya will follow up with quote.
[00:17:18] Ravi: ok great.
[00:17:25] Maya: thanks everyone - i'll send notes and links, and we'll schedule the benchmark kickoff.
[00:17:32] Alice: thanks all.
[00:17:35] [00:42:00] End of recording

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "redwood-gpt-1" spoken as "redwood g p t one"), and speaker attribution may be fuzzy in a few places. Links referenced: parity-mapping-sheet (link to be shared), security pack (link to be shared), example-shim-repo (link to be shared).
